Guile

GYL -- from Old French guile, related to 'wile.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Guile is sly or cunning intelligence used to deceive or manipulate.

Instead of confronting his rival directly, the young inventor used guile to trick him into revealing his secret formula during a friendly chat.

Worked Example

Over twenty years running the family shop, she had learned to negotiate with pure guile, always seeming to give in while quietly getting exactly the price she wanted.

Notice guile names an ongoing personal QUALITY -- a kind of cleverness someone has and uses again and again -- not one single trick. Compare Artifice, which can name one specific device or stratagem, like a hidden trapdoor.

How Guile Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

cunning

cunning: skill in deceiving or achieving one's goals craftily

craftiness

craftiness: cleverness used for a sly or deceptive purpose

Antonyms

innocence

innocence: a lack of guile or worldly cunning

honesty

honesty: truthfulness and directness in dealing with others

How Strong Is It? — craftiness → guile → cunning

craftiness vs. guile

craftiness vs. guile: Craftiness is milder than guile: a raccoon opening a trash can shows harmless craftiness, while guile is a deeper, sharper cunning aimed at deceiving people.

cunning vs. guile

cunning vs. guile: Cunning is stronger than guile: guile relies on sly cleverness, but a spy's cunning goes further, slipping false documents past three border checkpoints without raising suspicion.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — guile-

root — guile-: deceit, cunning trickery (Old French (guile), related to 'wile')

Put it together

Put it together: Guile comes from an Old French word for deceit, closely related to the English word 'wile.' At its root, guile has always meant a kind of clever, calculated dishonesty -- not brute force, but brainpower turned toward deception.

Use the root in a new word: beguile

Use the root in a new word: beguile: The con artist tried to beguile the elderly couple into signing over their savings with a string of flattering promises.

Root Check

Word Choice

Guile is an ongoing personal trait -- a kind of cunning someone has and uses repeatedly. Compare Artifice, which can refer to a single, specific clever trick or device, like a hidden mirror or false wall. A person with guile might rely on several different pieces of artifice over the years.
